items.stem: A vendor claims its AI will make a bank's lending decisions with near-perfect accuracy and no oversight. What is the soundest executive response?

options.text: Treat the certainty claim sceptically and insist on human oversight and responsible-AI controls
options.rationale: Correct: current AI is probabilistic and high-stakes decisions require oversight and governance.

options.text: Accept the claim since vendors validate their own models
options.rationale: Vendor self-validation is not sufficient assurance.
Speed without controls creates serious risk.

options.text: Avoid AI entirely because no claim can be trusted

items.explanation: Correct: current AI is probabilistic and high-stakes decisions require oversight and governance.

items.stem: Which TWO factors should most shape how an executive prioritises AI use cases? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The business value the use case would create
options.rationale: Correct: value is a primary prioritisation axis.

options.text: The feasibility given data, talent and technology readiness
options.rationale: Correct: feasibility determines whether value can actually be captured.

options.text: How impressive the demo looks to the board
options.rationale: Demo appeal is not a sound basis for prioritisation.

options.text: Whether a competitor announced something similar
options.rationale: Competitor noise is not a value or feasibility measure.

options.text: The novelty of the underlying algorithm
options.rationale: Novelty does not equal business value.

items.explanation: Correct: value is a primary prioritisation axis.

items.stem: A bank launches 30 disconnected AI pilots with no prioritisation; few reach production. What is the core strategic failure?

options.text: Absence of portfolio prioritisation and sequencing against value and feasibility
options.rationale: Correct: scattering effort without prioritisation and sequencing wastes resources and rarely scales.
The problem is lack of focus, not too few pilots.

options.text: AI simply cannot be deployed in banking
options.rationale: Banks deploy AI successfully with focus and governance.

options.text: Pilots should never be used for AI
options.rationale: Pilots are useful when prioritised and sequenced.

items.explanation: Correct: scattering effort without prioritisation and sequencing wastes resources and rarely scales.
